About the Physical Therapy event

Physical Therapy is a Health Professions event in the HOSA secondary division. Format: testing · skills.

Ten in-depth lessons following the HOSA Physical Therapy 2026–27 test plan (musculoskeletal, neuromuscular and pediatrics/older adults 16% each; profession, cardiopulmonary and integumentary 14% each; legal and ethical 10%) and all eight Round Two skills, built around Pierson and Fairchild, Pagliarulo, DHO: Health Science and APTA’s PT Moves Me videos. Includes device-fitting and gait-sequence drills, labeled joint, brain, skin, heart and lung diagrams, a rule-of-nines lab, PROM hand-placement cards and safety scenarios. Always follow the scenario and rating sheets you are given.

Sample Physical Therapy questions

1. Who is responsible for developing a patient’s physical therapy plan of care?

  1. The physical therapist assistant
  2. The physical therapist
  3. The PT aide
  4. The patient’s insurer
Show answer

B. The physical therapist

The PT examines the patient, sets goals and designs the plan of care. The PTA may provide treatment under it.

2. In the ICF model, a stroke survivor who can no longer attend her book club has a restriction in which component?

  1. Body structure
  2. Body function
  3. Health condition
  4. Participation
Show answer

D. Participation

The ICF model describes body functions and structures, activities (tasks) and participation (involvement in life situations), along with environmental and personal factors.

3. A patient who is non-weight-bearing on one leg uses crutches. Which gait pattern is used?

  1. Four-point gait
  2. Two-point gait
  3. Three-point gait
  4. Swing-to gait with both legs
Show answer

C. Three-point gait

In a three-point gait, both crutches and the affected leg move forward together, then the unaffected leg steps through, keeping weight off the injured leg.
